newsitem.title: KENYA: New report expected on murder of Briton in Kenya.
newsitem.headline: New report expected on murder of Briton in Kenya.

text.p: A new report on the murder of British tourist Julie Ward nine years ago should be released by Kenya's attorney-general later this week, according to her father.

John Ward, who has spent more than $500,000 and made over 50 trips to Kenya campaigning for his daughter's death to be properly investigated, told Reuters he expected the report to be made public on Saturday.
"I don't know yet what it will say or if it will name suspects," said Ward, a British hotelier who helped with the latest investigation. "I only know of my contribution to it."
Julie Ward's mutilated remains were found in a remote corner of the Masai Mara game reserve, 200 kms (125 miles) south of the capital in September 1988.
Kenyan police said originally that she had been killed by wild animals, but her father's dogged campaign finally led to a series of investigations.
Two game rangers charged with the murder were acquitted in 1992 by a high court judge who said Kenyan police were attempting to cover up the crime.
The latest investigation began in March last year.
